hero.title: Every access is a 0 or a 1. We make it the right one.
hero.description: Qubital is an identity & access management consultancy. We help organisations control who and what can access their systems, from privileged accounts and identity governance to customer, workforce and AI agent identities.

home.statement: Our name comes from the qubit, which can be 0 and 1 at the same time. Access can't. Every login, every permission, every action of an AI agent ends in one decision: granted or denied. We make sure each one is right.

practice.title: Access, decided in seconds.
practice.description: A new colleague needs access. Policy checks run on their own, the manager approves with one click, and everything is logged for the audit.

pam.title: Privileged Access Management (PAM)
pam.short: Secure, control and monitor the accounts with the most powerful rights.
pam.description: Privileged accounts are the top target in almost every attack. We help you discover them, vault their credentials, enforce just-in-time access and record sessions, so admin rights are only used when needed and always traceable.

iga.title: Identity Governance & Administration (IGA)
iga.short: Everyone has exactly the access they need, and you can prove it.
iga.description: We automate the identity lifecycle from joiner to leaver, build role models that fit your organisation, and set up access reviews and reporting that satisfy auditors without overloading your managers.

ciam.title: Customer Identity (CIAM)
ciam.short: Seamless, secure sign-in experiences your customers trust.
ciam.description: Registration, login and consent shape the first impression of your digital products. We design customer identity that is frictionless for users, resilient against account takeover and compliant with GDPR.

wiam.title: Workforce Identity (WIAM)
wiam.short: One secure identity for every employee, on every app and device.
wiam.description: We give your workforce single sign-on, strong multi-factor authentication and conditional access, connecting cloud and on-premises applications into one consistent identity layer built on Zero Trust.

ai.title: Non-Human Identity (NHI) and AI Agent Identity Governance
ai.short: Govern service accounts, API keys, bots and AI agents like any other identity.
ai.description: Service accounts, API keys, certificates, bots and now AI agents: non-human identities usually outnumber your people, and many have no clear owner. We bring them under identity governance: a full inventory, clear ownership, tightly scoped and short-lived credentials, and an audit trail for everything they do.
points: Inventory of non-human identities & AI agents

items.q: Do you work with small and mid-sized companies?
items.a: Absolutely. Identity security matters at every size. We scale our approach, from a focused assessment to a full programme, to your organisation and budget.

items.a: Yes. Identity and access controls are central to NIS2, DORA and ISO 27001. We assess where you stand, close the gaps and help you produce the evidence auditors ask for.

hero.title: Named after the qubit. Built on clarity.
hero.description: Qubital was founded in Germany with a clear focus: identity is the new security perimeter, and it deserves specialists.

story.title: Why Qubital?
paragraphs: A classical bit is either 0 or 1. A qubit, the building block of quantum computers, can be both at once until it is measured. It holds every possibility at the same time.

That is how we approach a project. Before we commit to a solution, we keep the options open, listen carefully and explore what is possible. When the picture is clear, we decide and build with precision.
Qubital combines qubit and digital. In identity security that balance is everything: access has to be easy enough for people to do their work, and strict enough to keep attackers out.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction and controller
body: Thank you for your interest in our website. Protecting your personal data matters to us. This privacy policy explains which personal data we process when you use this website, for which purposes and on which legal basis, and which rights you have.
The controller within the meaning of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is:
Qubital GmbH

If you have any questions about data protection, you can reach us at any time at the email address above.

sections.heading: 2. Data collected when you visit our website
body: ## 2.1 Server log files

When you visit our website for information only, without contacting us, your browser automatically sends data to the server that delivers the website. This data is stored in server log files: the IP address of the requesting device, the date and time of access, the page or file requested, the website from which you were referred, the browser and operating system used, and the amount of data transferred.

We use this data to deliver the website, to keep it stable and secure, and to detect and prevent misuse. The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR; our legitimate interest lies in these purposes. The data is not combined with other data sources and is not used to identify you. Log files are deleted automatically after a short period, unless they are needed to investigate a specific security incident.
## 2.2 Encryption

For security reasons and to protect confidential content, such as enquiries you send us, this website uses SSL/TLS encryption. You can recognise an encrypted connection by "https://" in your browser’s address bar and the lock symbol. With encryption active, the data you send us cannot be read by third parties.

sections.heading: 3. Hosting and content delivery
body: This website is hosted by Vercel Inc., 440 N Barranca Ave #4133, Covina, CA 91723, USA. Vercel operates a global content delivery network, so the website can be delivered from a server close to you. In doing so, Vercel processes the data described in section 2.1 on our behalf.

Vercel acts as our processor under a data processing agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR. The legal basis for using Vercel is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR; our legitimate interest is the secure, fast and reliable provision of our website. Transfers to the USA are based on the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses or an adequacy decision such as the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.

sections.heading: 4. Cookies and local storage
body: Cookies are small text files that your browser stores on your device. This website uses no tracking or marketing cookies.

We set one technically necessary cookie, NEXT_LOCALE. It contains only your language (for example "de" or "en") and is used solely to show the website in the language you chose. In addition, your chosen colour theme (light or dark) is stored in your browser’s local storage. Neither is used to track you or shared with third parties.

The legal basis is § 25 (2) No. 2 TDDDG, as this storage is strictly necessary to provide the website you requested, together with Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR. You can delete cookies and local storage in your browser settings at any time or block them; the website will then use its default language and theme.
Because we use no cookies or similar technologies that require consent, we do not show a cookie banner.

sections.heading: 5. Contacting us
body: ## 5.1 Contact form

If you send us a message via the contact form, we process the data you enter: your name, email address, organisation (optional), the topic you select and your message. We use this data only to handle your enquiry and any follow-up questions. You will also receive an automatic confirmation of receipt by email.

The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR where your enquiry relates to a contract or to pre-contractual measures, and otherwise Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR; our legitimate interest lies in responding to enquiries addressed to us. Emails from the contact form are sent through our Microsoft 365 mailbox, provided by Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited, acting as our processor under Art. 28 GDPR. Where Microsoft transfers data to the USA, this is based on the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses or the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.
## 5.2 Email
If you contact us by email, we process your email address and the information contained in your message in order to answer it. The legal basis is the same as for the contact form (section 5.1).
We delete the data from your enquiry once it has been dealt with and is no longer needed, unless statutory retention obligations apply, for example under commercial or tax law.

sections.heading: 6. Web analytics
body: To understand how our website is used and to improve it, we use Azure Application Insights, a service of Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited. The data is stored in a Microsoft data centre in Germany (region Germany West Central), and Microsoft acts as our processor under Art. 28 GDPR.

Application Insights is configured on this website so that no cookies, local storage or other identifiers are stored on your device. It records which pages are viewed and basic technical information about the visit, such as the browser, the device type and the approximate location (country and city) derived from your IP address. The IP address itself is not stored. Browsers that send a Do Not Track signal are not recorded. The resulting statistics are pseudonymous, are kept for 90 days and are not used to identify you.

The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR; our legitimate interest lies in the anonymous evaluation of how our website is used. You can object to this processing at any time (see section 8.2), for example by enabling Do Not Track in your browser.

sections.heading: 7. Website functions
body: ## 7.1 Fonts
All fonts on this website are delivered from our own hosting. No connection to external font providers, such as Google Fonts, is established when you visit the website.
## 7.2 Images and animations
All images and animations on this website are delivered from our own hosting. We do not embed content from third-party platforms, such as video services or social networks.

sections.heading: 8. Your rights
body: ## 8.1 Rights under the GDPR

You have the right to access your personal data (Art. 15 GDPR), to rectification (Art. 16 GDPR), to erasure (Art. 17 GDPR), to restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR), to notification (Art. 19 GDPR) and to data portability (Art. 20 GDPR). Where processing is based on your consent, you can withdraw it at any time with effect for the future (Art. 7 (3) GDPR). To exercise these rights, simply write to hello@qubital.eu.

You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR). The authority responsible for us is the Bavarian State Office for Data Protection Supervision (BayLDA), Promenade 18, 91522 Ansbach, Germany.
## 8.2 Right to object

Where we process your personal data on the basis of our legitimate interests (Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR), you have the right to object to this processing at any time on grounds relating to your particular situation (Art. 21 GDPR). We will then no longer process the data unless we can demonstrate compelling legitimate grounds that override your interests, rights and freedoms, or the processing serves the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims.

sections.heading: 9. Storage duration
body: We store personal data only for as long as is necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, or as long as statutory retention periods require. Sections 2 to 6 describe the storage periods for the individual processing activities. Once the purpose no longer applies and no retention obligation exists, the data is deleted.

sections.heading: 10. Changes to this privacy policy
body: We update this privacy policy when our website, our services or the legal requirements change. The current version is always available on this page.
